def sum_units_score_at_least_25(entries):
    """Walk the fish room at closing time and settle the supplement ledger for
    the display tanks. All evening you have been moving down the aisle with a
    clipboard, pausing at each aquarium to check the glass, test the water,
    and note what the tank will need before the lights go out. Now the rounds
    are done and the clipboard has come back to the bench as a single list
    called entries, one row per tank you visited. Each element of entries is
    a list of exactly three values: a label (str), a score (int), and a
    factor (int). Read the label as the name taped to the tank stand, the
    score as the condition rating you assigned after the water test, and the
    factor as the number of conditioner units that particular tank consumes
    whenever it gets a full treatment. House policy is simple: only tanks in
    solid shape get dosed tonight, and a tank counts as being in solid shape
    when its rating reaches the cutoff of twenty-five. Go through the list
    one row at a time, keep the tanks that make the cutoff, and add up how
    much conditioner you must draw from the supply cabinet for them. Return
    the sum of factor over the entries whose score is greater than or equal
    to 25 (0 if none qualify). Log that single number on the closing sheet,
    restock the cabinet, and dim the room lights on your way out; an empty
    clipboard simply means no conditioner leaves the cabinet tonight.

    >>> sum_units_score_at_least_25([])
    0
    >>> sum_units_score_at_least_25([['Ana', 25, 5]])
    5
    """
